questions.q: In the three-stage pipeline, what does StartCrawler accomplish before RunETLJob begins?
options: It refreshes the Glue Data Catalog's schema for newly-landed data, so the ETL job reads current metadata
It deletes the raw data so the ETL job starts clean
It provisions the Lambda function used later
It has no functional purpose besides logging
questions.explain: The crawler runs first so the Data Catalog reflects the current schema of the raw data before the ETL job transforms it.

questions.q: In the example state machine, both StartCrawler and RunETLJob Catch into the same NotifyFailure state. Why is that a reasonable pattern?
options: One shared fallback handles a failure at either stage, instead of duplicating near-identical notification logic per stage
ASL requires every state machine to have exactly one Catch target
It disables retries for both stages
It's required because Lambda can only be invoked once per state machine
questions.explain: Sharing a fallback state is a common, sensible production pattern — one notification path instead of copy-pasted failure handling in each stage.

questions.q: What is the main argument this lesson makes against just having one Lambda invoke the next to chain crawler, ETL, and notification steps?
options: Retry logic, timeouts, and failure branching end up scattered across function code, invisible from outside, with no single view of where an execution stopped
Lambda functions cannot call the Glue API under any circumstances
AWS technically forbids one Lambda from invoking another
It would be cheaper to use Step Functions in every case, with no tradeoffs
questions.explain: The core argument is about visibility and declarative control — not that chaining Lambdas is technically impossible, but that it hides the orchestration logic instead of surfacing it in a console-visible state machine.

questions.q: Which Resource ARN pattern starts a Glue crawler directly from a Task state, without a wrapper Lambda?
options: arn:aws:states:::aws-sdk:glue:startCrawler
arn:aws:lambda:::glue:startCrawler
arn:aws:states:::wait:startCrawler
Crawlers cannot be started from Step Functions at all
questions.explain: Step Functions has direct AWS SDK service integrations, including for Glue's startCrawler API, callable without an intermediary Lambda.

questions.q: What does the Step Functions console execution diagram let you see for a completed run of this pipeline?
options: The actual path the execution took through the states, with input/output at each hop, including exactly where a failure occurred if one did
Only the total dollar cost of the execution
Nothing — Step Functions does not retain execution history
Only the Lambda function's CloudWatch Logs, with no state-level detail
questions.explain: Standard workflow executions keep a full, visual, state-by-state history — exactly what makes it possible to answer "did last night's pipeline finish, and if not, where did it stop?"
